tracks.title: Reignition: Lights Up on Progress Street
tracks.loreNote: Thematically answering the sign-off of 2004's "Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street" ("Lights out on Progress Street... Goodnight, Forger Nation"), the opening anthem of 2015's *Reignition* celebrates the end of the band's decade-long **2005–2014 Burnout Hiatus**. Opening with warm acoustic piano chords that erupt into Cassidy's bright analog polyphonic analog brass fanfare, Tyler's booming gated-reverb snare, Evan's driving eighth-note bassline, and Ryan's soaring electric guitar, it marks the family's triumphant return to full-throttle 1980s AOR studio rock.

As Cassidy sings over a sequenced analog bassline, nine-tenths of the family's $2.4B+ fortress sits permanently beneath the waterline where the outside world can never see it.

tracks.title: Ten Years in the Quiet
tracks.loreNote: An honest, deeply moving 84 BPM 1980s AOR power ballad reflecting on the **2005–2014 Burnout Hiatus**. After recording four studio albums in four years and reaching complete sensory and physical exhaustion at the end of the 2004 Norfolk tour, Ryan and Cassidy sing about how choosing to walk away from the spotlight for ten years—drinking coffee on the Progress Street porch, cooking family dinners, and protecting their neurodivergent boundaries—saved their lives and kept the five of them whole.

tracks.title: Fifty-Two to Nothing: The Norfolk Reckoning
tracks.loreNote: Written and recorded in a burst of autumn excitement in October 2015 immediately after **Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI)** traveled down to Norfolk for **Virginia Dominion University (VDU)**'s Homecoming game. After VDU students printed thousands of mocking *"38–0"* t-shirts commemorating their 2014 upset, the Forgers walked into Norfolk and delivered a triumphant **52–0 shutout victory**. Featuring Tyler's thunderous marching snare cadence and a roaring stadium chorus, it became an instant autumn anthem across Blacksburg.
